name: Basophils (%)
rangeNote: No lower limit is used: basophils are the rarest white cells and 0 % is normal. Because there are so few, small changes are often chance.
summary: Basophils are the rarest white blood cells. They release histamine and take part in allergic reactions and inflammation. This value is their share of all white cells.

high.meaning: A slightly higher share is usually a reaction to allergies or long-lasting inflammation. A share that stays clearly raised, especially with other changes in the blood count, is worth discussing with your doctor, because rarely it comes from a bone marrow condition.
commonCauses: Long-lasting inflammation, such as inflammatory bowel disease
Bone marrow conditions such as chronic myeloid leukaemia (rare)

low.meaning: A low share means nothing on its own. Basophils are so few that a result of 0 % is common in healthy people.
